narrative: The model estimates an 82% chance you will leave your job, which is why you were denied a promotion: the organization is treating the promotion as an investment likely to be lost soon. The strongest signal is your total work experience. At 6–10 years overall, you sit above the most common staying profile of 1–5 years, suggesting a more mobile, experienced employee, and this factor pushed most strongly toward leaving. Your time in the current organization, 1–5 years, was the second strongest influence and also leaned toward leaving; although many staying employees share this tenure, in your combination of circumstances it added to the flight risk. The third key signal is that you have other job opportunities. Only about a quarter of employees predicted to stay report having alternatives, so your “yes” here substantially increased the concern that you may move. These signals outweigh stabilizing factors in your profile. Before revisiting promotion, discuss concrete retention steps: clearer promotion criteria, compensation and recognition review, support for psychological exhaustion and job stability, and whether internal growth can compete with outside offers. You should also assess whether the role, pay, and development path meet your goals; if not, an open conversation can clarify expectations on both sides.
